messages:
maria: kicking off eviction-policy sweep across regions + GPU families :chart_with_upwards_trend:

maria: goal: understand KV cache hit rate vs 99p latency under real seqlen mix (session-weighted). Compare LRU, LFU, size-aware LRU, and a 2-tier hot/cold evict scheme.

maria: test matrix:
- models: rwkv-14b-ggml (fp16), redwood-7b-v2 (int8 quant)
- gpus: A10G(us-west-2) vs H100(eu-central-1)
- seqlen distributions: short-heavy (chat), bimodal (summarization+chat), long-tail (code)
- concurrency: 50, 200

aj: nice. can you paste the exact command used for the run?

maria: sure, run script (one-liner):
```bash
./bench/kv_sweep.sh \
  --model redwood-7b-v2 --quant int8 \
  --gpus A10G,H100 --regions us-west-2,eu-central-1 \
  --seqlens short,bimodal,longtail \
  --concurrency 50,200 \
  --evict LRU,LFU,SLRU,2tier --out s3://redwood-bench/1767894321/\
```

kevin: got the CSVs from s3, quick summary first pass:
- 2-tier consistently improved hit rate ~5-9% vs plain LRU on the long-tail mix
- H100 had 10-15% lower 99p token latency for cache hits but similar miss latency
- int8 quant model increased base token latency ~4ms on A10G, but improved throughput when combined with batching

maria: attaching distilled numbers (pasted):
short-heavy @50c: LRU hit 78%, 99p=120ms (A10G), LFU 80% 99p=115ms, 2-tier 85% 99p=98ms
bimodal @200c: LRU 65% 99p=210ms (H100), LFU 68% 99p=195ms, SLRU 72% 99p=170ms
longtail @200c: LRU 42% 99p=420ms (A10G paging spikes), 2-tier 51% 99p=320ms, LFU 46% 99p=390ms

sophia: do we have eviction churn numbers? i.e., megabytes evicted/sec or keys/sec?

maria: yes, churn: longtail @200c LRU=9.8MB/s evicted, 2-tier hot-only evict=4.1MB/s, LFU=7.2MB/s. Lower churn correlated with lower 99p.

aj: interesting that H100 had lower hit 99p improvements despite better raw perf. maybe kernel choices or memcpy path?

kevin: noticed different kernel selector on H100 for the attention matmul that reduced perp mem copies for KV loads. but cold-path miss still dominated by CPU->GPU page fault handling in our paging implementation.

maria: reproduced an example stack trace for a paging spike:
```
[2026-02-14T15:04:21Z] evictor: page_in_fail -> falling back to sync page copy
[2026-02-14T15:04:21Z] gpu0: stall 32ms on kv_load (cpu fallback)
[2026-02-14T15:04:21Z] metrics: token_latency_ms p99=512
```

sophia: any OOMs?

maria: we hit transient OOMs on A10G on the longtail @200c with LRU when cache_size default (12GB) was set; bumping cache to 16GB removed OOMs but at cost of infra footprint. 2-tier allowed keeping effective hot-reserve smaller and avoided OOMs.

aj: kernel choice note: on H100 we default to cuBLASLt kernels for fused attention; those kernels seem to be more tolerant of random KV loads. On A10G we use cutlass variants that benefit from sequential accesses. explains region/gpu diff.

kevin: suggestion: add a simple seqlen-aware eviction: temporarily favor small-seq keys for retention under high concurrency. Implementation: add weight = key_size * (1 + alpha * avg_seq_len_bucket). I can prototype.

maria: yep, that would help chat-heavy flows. also need to run the same sweep with a quantized kv-store (store keys compressed) — earlier tests showed ~6% hit lift due to fitting more entries in cache.

infra-bot: job 1767894321-kv-sweep finished. artifacts: s3://redwood-bench/1767894321/{metrics.csv,evict_stats.json,events.log} :white_check_mark:

aj: next steps:
- kevin to prototype seqlen-weighted eviction (PR by EOD)
- maria to rerun longtail @200c with compressed-kv + 2-tier in both regions
- sophia to add eviction churn counters to perf dashboard (per-region)

sophia: adding dashboard panels now, will include region comparison and kernel selector tag.

kevin: quick note on evaluation: when presenting to product, show both unit economics (tokens/$) and 99p latency delta — customers care about tail latency more than mean.

maria: thanks everyone. sharing final CSVs and a short slide for tomorrow's eng-ml sync. :rocket:
